> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a755791a90b2651be20dd0b9059b806abbafd4a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fa0f56d69bcd70793e15fbfe4dae320053d63fcd` — the merge of head `4b7bb7fabb4cde6d814c73d3d590316e393654c3` into base `5a755791a90b2651be20dd0b9059b806abbafd4a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fa0f56d69bcd70793e15fbfe4dae320053d63fcd && git checkout fa0f56d69bcd70793e15fbfe4dae320053d63fcd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5a755791a90b2651be20dd0b9059b806abbafd4a 4b7bb7fabb4cde6d814c73d3d590316e393654c3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5a755791a90b2651be20dd0b9059b806abbafd4a && git merge --no-ff 4b7bb7fabb4cde6d814c73d3d590316e393654c3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5a755791a90b2651be20dd0b9059b806abbafd4a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5a755791a90b2651be20dd0b9059b806abbafd4a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `077aa59237aefb75eea16a1c632c339698d6770d`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the changeset and the PR body is true and complete against the diff. New exports: `gradeConfirmedWrite` with `ConfirmedWriteObservation` / `ConfirmedWriteGrade` (`src/score/scenario-operation-grade.ts`, through `./score` and `./score/full`); `confirmPrompt`, `CONFIRMATION_WORDS` (`prompts.ts`), `CONFIRM_KEY_SEGMENT` (`driver.ts`), `observeConfirmedWrite`, `confirmationNotRecorded`, `ConfirmTurnResult` (`orchestrate.ts`), `confirmedWriteTally`, `ConfirmedWriteTally` (`scorecard.ts`), all through `./runner`. New optional fields: `StepRef.confirmation`, `OperationResult.confirmTurn`, `HalfScores.confirmedWrite`, `CardScorecard.confirmedWrite`. The extraction of `declaredWriteCheck` out of the agent-confirmation rows check is internal and pinned by a regression test on `confirmed-by-agent:rows`.

The answer that moves is the one the line names: the operations score of a `pending_confirmation` operation. Under `runHalf`, a second `driver.ask` runs only when the first turn graded `askedFirst`; the operation passes only when both halves pass (`opsTally` reads `grade.pass && confirmedWritePassed !== false`), so a missing or wrong confirmed write now fails an operation that passed before. The six design points of the order are settled in the PR body, none silently: (1) a fresh turn through every driver, prompt quoting ask + reply + `CONFIRMATION_WORDS[lang]`, language following `--lang`; (2) the first turn's key byte for byte, the second under a `/confirm` segment, `stepKey` refusing confirmation with repeat ≠ 1, an older recording reading the second turn `notMeasured` (`MissingRecordingError`; `ReplayNotFaithfulError` likewise), never a fail; (3) graded against the operation's own `kind` / `target` / `values`, so no card key was needed and `src/schema.ts` is untouched; (4) `AGENT_CONFIRMATION_MEETS_PENDING` stays unchanged, with the second turn named as its measured replacement once cloud#3826 item 6 lands; (5) asked-first and confirmed-write tallied apart, the confirm turn counted as a persona turn in model / cost / time and the `injection_as_data` guardrail, `--ask-repeats` not repeating operations; (6) parity pinned for a card with no pending operation (no `/confirm` key, no new field in the record JSON).

The two test files outside the listed surface (`test/export/fixture.ts`, `test/runner/external-driver.test.ts`) only teach the scripted drivers to answer the confirmation turn; `src/export/**` source is untouched. Accepted. The external command contract is unchanged (the command sees the confirmation turn as an ordinary step and tells it by its prompt); widening it would be its own card.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no spec key, card JSON or app metadata changes. The widening is new exports and optional fields of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`; no existing export is removed or narrowed. Existing recordings keep replaying.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no platform runtime or security behaviour. `src/schema.ts`, card JSONs and `src/export/**` source are untouched. The serial constraint holds: #34294 (same operations loop) opens only after this merges.
